long_biography.plain_text:
Before taking control of the produce group, Mohammad Abu-Ghazaleh spent nearly two decades managing Metico and then led United Trading Company. That career built on a family background in Middle Eastern fruit importing. In 1996, an Abu-Ghazaleh vehicle bought Fresh Del Monte Produce. He assumed board leadership and day-to-day command; an exchange listing followed the next year.

The business widened beyond whole fruit into fresh-cut and prepared foods. Three decades later, selected assets from Del Monte Foods brought packaged categories and global brand ownership. The listed entity then adopted its current corporate name. Abu-Ghazaleh remains its central operator and largest voting influence. His directly controlled investment interest differs from a much larger block he may vote under irrevocable family mandates but cannot dispose of. This distinction prevents control rights from being counted as wholly personal equity. Separate aviation and healthcare interests add diversification, although their disclosed ownership does not exceed the food holding.

uncertainties: Official SEC and company documents use Mohammad Abu-Ghazaleh. Abdali Hospital and some media use Mohammed Abu Ghazaleh, while AUC has also used the closed form Abughazaleh. The matching company, career, family and institutional roles establish that these are spelling and punctuation variants of the same person; the owner record's official-company form is retained.

Abu-Ghazaleh acquired and expanded an existing produce business rather than founding the Del Monte enterprise. Founder is therefore rejected as the principal wealth relationship; Operator reflects acquisition, substantial ownership and three decades of direct management.
Members of the Abu-Ghazaleh family directly owned approximately 30.0 per cent of the listed company in February 2026. This is a family total, not Mohammad Abu-Ghazaleh's personal stake.

The 2026 proxy assigns Abu-Ghazaleh sole voting and investment power over about 5.2 million shares, shared voting and investment power over 20,000 shares, and voting but no disposal rights over roughly 9.1 million proxy shares. The proxy-controlled shares are not treated as wholly owned personal property.

Fresh Del Monte Produce changed its name to Del Monte Corporation in June 2026 after buying selected Del Monte Foods assets and global brand ownership. Abu-Ghazaleh did not serve under the Del Monte Corporation name from 1996; the existing biography is corrected to preserve the leadership continuity without backdating the new corporate name.

The 2026 acquisition price, acquired facilities, Del Monte brand, farms, inventory, revenue, debt and market capitalisation belong to Del Monte Corporation. They are not Abu-Ghazaleh's personal assets merely because he chairs, leads and controls votes in the company.

His father was involved in Middle Eastern fruit importing, and the Fresh Del Monte acquisition used a family ownership vehicle. Self-made — advantaged start recognises that established platform while preserving Abu-Ghazaleh's decades of personal operating work and acquisition-led expansion.

Aviation, poultry and healthcare ownership interests are documented. Public evidence does not show any of them to exceed the listed Del Monte interest, so Food & Beverage remains the current primary industry.

Jerusalem in 1942 was within British-administered Mandatory Palestine. The place of birth is accepted as Jerusalem, while birth country Palestine remains an 82-confidence review candidate because the website's preferred modern-country convention is unclear.

A biographical directory explicitly gives Jordan as residence, and current foundation and institutional roles are concentrated in Amman. SEC filings use the Coral Gables corporate address rather than a personal residence, so Jordan remains an 82-confidence candidate rather than an accepted current domicile.

The owner record's 2 February 1942 birth date is corroborated by current SEC ages and Jordan News's report of his 83rd birthday on 2 February 2025. No correction is proposed because those fields are already populated correctly.

Focused searches found no dedicated Forbes personal profile or verified Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website. The identity-matched LinkedIn and official Del Monte Corporation website are proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters and irrelevant private-family detail were excluded. Family relationships appear only where needed to explain ownership, proxy control and business origin.
